name: Rezin
overview: Rezin was a king of Syria who played a prominent role in opposing the southern kingdom of Judah during the reign of Ahaz, as recorded in Isaiah 7:1. His alliance with Pekah of Israel to wage war against Jerusalem ultimately failed, and God promised to set adversaries against him, uniting his enemies as a form of divine judgment (Isaiah 9:11). Additionally, Rezin's name appears among the returned Babylonian captives, indicating that some of his descendants were part of the post-exilic community restoring Israel (Ezra 2:48; Nehemiah 7:50). The prophetic warnings and historical records together illustrate Rezin's significance both as an enemy of God's people and as part of their eventual restoration.
